# Trace Statistics

*Generated by `scripts/gen-trace-stats.ts` from real runs. Generation times are measurements, taken by `npm run measure` and stored in `reports/trace-timing.json`; everything else is regenerated and checked in CI. Do not edit by hand.*

## Headline

- One epoch of the **“A single neuron”** experiment (4 examples, batch size 4) decomposes into **57 individually inspectable, individually explained operations** across six levels of granularity; the full 60-epoch run has 3,422.
- One epoch of the **“Activation functions”** experiment (10 examples, batch size 10) decomposes into **123 individually inspectable, individually explained operations** across six levels of granularity; the full 40-epoch run has 4,922.
- One epoch of the **“Forward propagation”** experiment (40 examples, batch size 8) decomposes into **879 individually inspectable, individually explained operations** across six levels of granularity; the full 20-epoch run has 17,584.
- One epoch of the **“Loss functions”** experiment (40 examples, batch size 10) decomposes into **480 individually inspectable, individually explained operations** across six levels of granularity; the full 30-epoch run has 14,402.
- One epoch of the **“Gradient descent”** experiment (50 examples, batch size 50) decomposes into **563 individually inspectable, individually explained operations** across six levels of granularity; the full 40-epoch run has 22,522.
- One epoch of the **“Back-propagation”** experiment (24 examples, batch size 4) decomposes into **574 individually inspectable, individually explained operations** across six levels of granularity; the full 30-epoch run has 17,224.
- One epoch of the **“XOR needs a hidden layer”** experiment (4 examples, batch size 4) decomposes into **99 individually inspectable, individually explained operations** across six levels of granularity; the full 150-epoch run has 14,854.
- One epoch of the **“A CNN on handwritten digits”** experiment (1500 examples, batch size 20) decomposes into **41,929 individually inspectable, individually explained operations** across six levels of granularity; the full 3-epoch run has 125,791.
- One epoch of the **“Vanishing gradients”** experiment (64 examples, batch size 16) decomposes into **5,544 individually inspectable, individually explained operations** across six levels of granularity; the full 20-epoch run has 110,898.
- One epoch of the **“Learning-rate pathology”** experiment (50 examples, batch size 50) decomposes into **563 individually inspectable, individually explained operations** across six levels of granularity; the full 30-epoch run has 16,892.

Every one of these instructions can be stepped to, has its full numerical result stored (or recomputable from a checkpoint), and is explained by a generated general formula, a formula with its own numbers substituted, and a plain-language sentence.

## Scaling

Instruction count is linear in epochs and in examples per epoch (per-sample execution), grows with depth by a constant number of instructions per layer, and is independent of layer width — width changes the size of each instruction's tensors (trace bytes), not their number. Batch size changes only the per-batch overhead (begin/end, loss reduction and one update block per parameter per batch).
